PROVIDENCE DAY SCHOOL CHARGERS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Academic & Competitive Programs
Research Area — Clubs that compete regionally and nationally
A deep 15-club competitive slate: DECA (state fi nationals 2026) co-flagship, a full civic cluster (Speech & Debate, Mock
Trial, Model U.N., World Quest, Quiz Bowl), a STEM cluster, and a standout business/economics strand. Only Academic
Decathlon is absent.
AT A GLANCE
Co-flagship DECA — advanced from the state career development conference to the
national ICDC in 2026.
Civic cluster Speech & Debate, Mock Trial, Model U.N., World Quest, and Quiz Bowl.
STEM cluster Science Olympiad, Robotics Team, Technology Student Association, Drone
Club, Build Your Own Boat.
Business/economics DECA, Future Business Leaders of America, Euro Challenge, PD Economics
Challenge.
Health & esports HOSA (health) and a competitive E-Sports Club.
Verification note Club existence is confirmed by the official list; specific event placements are
largely not public.
Clubs That Compete
Providence Day fields one of the deepest non-sport, non-arts competitive slates in the series — fifteen
team-oriented/competitive clubs on the official Upper School list, spanning business, civic, STEM, health,
economics, and global competition. DECA is the competitive co-flagship; a strong civic cluster (Speech &
Debate, Mock Trial, Model U.N., World Quest, Quiz Bowl) sits right behind it. [Source: Providence Day School —
Upper School Club List '25–26]
DECA — The Competitive Co-Flagship
DECA is Providence Day's standout academic-competition club, preparing students for marketing, finance,
hospitality, management, and entrepreneurship through role-plays, case studies, and prepared events, and
advancing from chartered-association (state) competition to the International Career Development Conference.
In 2026, Providence Day's DECA club shined at the state competition and qualified for nationals (ICDC,
held in Atlanta that April). [Source: providenceday.org — news, March 2026; DECA Inc.]
Verification limit: the School confirms the state success and advance to nationals but does not publicly itemize the specific DECA events
entered or final ICDC placements, so none are claimed here.
The Civic / Public-Voice Competitive Cluster
Providence Day carries a full civic-competition cluster — a correction worth stating plainly, since an earlier draft
of this research (before the official list was obtained) had understated it:
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
PROVIDENCE DAY SCHOOL CHARGERS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Club What it is
Speech & Debate Interscholastic competitive speech and debate (a full team, beyond the School's annual
speech contest).
Mock Trial Simulated courtroom-trial competition involving case preparation and advocacy.
Model UN Model United Nations diplomacy and resolution debate at conferences.
World Quest Current-affairs, geography, and global-knowledge competition.
Quiz Bowl Buzzer-based, fast-recall academic quiz competition.
Source: Upper School Club List '25–26. These five confirm a civic-competition depth not visible in pre-list public sources.
STEM & Engineering Competition
The STEM competition cluster includes Science Olympiad (team STEM events), the Robotics Team, the
Technology Student Association (TSA), the Drone Club, and the Build Your Own Boat engineering
challenge. Together they give students multiple applied-engineering and applied-science competitive outlets,
reinforced by the Middle School's IDEAS makerspaces. [Source: Upper School Club List '25–26]
Business & Economics Competition
Beyond DECA, Providence Day offers a notably deep business/economics competition strand: Future Business
Leaders of America (FBLA), the Euro Challenge (European-economics competition), and the PD Economics
Challenge. Combined with the Investment Management Society, Microfinance Club, and Investment Board
(covered in the catalog and thematic dossiers), this gives Providence Day a business and finance identity
unusual among peer schools. [Source: Upper School Club List '25–26]
Health & Esports
HOSA (Health Occupations Students of America) provides a competitive pathway for students interested in
health and medical careers, and the E-Sports Club offers competitive video-gaming (retained in scope for this
series). [Source: Upper School Club List '25–26]
What Is Not Evident
After vetting against the official list, the remaining genuine absences are narrow: there is no Academic
Decathlon team on the Upper School list. (Earlier notes that Mock Trial and Quiz Bowl were 'not evident' were
based on incomplete public sources and are now corrected — both exist.) Specific competition placements
across these clubs are largely not published, so this dossier reports the competitive slate at the program level
rather than with standings. [Source: Upper School Club List '25–26]
Source List
1. Providence Day School — Upper School Club List '25–26 (official roster of competitive clubs).
2. Providence Day School — news: DECA state success and advance to nationals (March 2026).
3. DECA Inc. — ICDC (Atlanta, April 25–28, 2026) for competition structure/context.
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 2

Club Catalog & Descriptions
Research Area — Non-sport, non-arts clubs and activities, TK–12
From the official Upper School Club List '25–26: 82 organizations, 77 in scope (including recreational sport clubs and the
student sports-media outlet); only 5 arts clubs excluded. A deep slate spanning a 15-club competitive roster, 9 affinity
groups, a strong business/finance cluster, and broad service, STEM, and recreational offerings.
AT A GLANCE
Official list size 82 Upper School organizations on the School's '25–26 list.

the student sports-media outlet; only the arts are excluded.

Scope & Methodology
This dossier catalogs Providence Day School Upper School clubs and activities outside athletics and the arts,
drawn directly from the School's official Upper School Club List '25–26. The list provides club names (and
internal advisor/leader contacts, which are intentionally omitted here); it does not publish per-club descriptions,
so the 'general focus' column gives a concise, generic descriptor derived from each club's name and activity type
rather than an invented Providence Day claim. Where a club's purpose is not self-evident, the focus is marked as
not specified. [Source: Providence Day School — Upper School Club List '25–26]
Scope boundaries (applied consistently): only performing-, literary-, and visual-arts clubs are excluded, as
arts. Recreational sport-interest clubs and the student sports-media outlet (PDSN) are included in this
series (per the producer's direction): the athletics series covers only competitive interscholastic teams, so casual
sport clubs and a sports-broadcast club would otherwise fall between the two series. E-sports is also in scope.
Grade band: Upper School = grades 9–12.

List '25–26]

sections.text:
PROVIDENCE DAY SCHOOL CHARGERS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Governance, Formation, Funding & Discovery
Research Area — How clubs are run, started, funded, and found
The official list confirms students start new clubs every year, each with a faculty advisor and student leaders, governed by
elected Student and Honor Councils. Funding process and a named club fair remain unpublished — reported as honest
gaps, with the low 57% funding sentiment flagged.
AT A GLANCE
Formation — The official list states students initiate the creation of new clubs each year.
confirmed
Advising Each club has faculty advisor(s) plus student leaders; clubs are student-led.
Governance bodies Elected Student Council and Honor Council; Foundation Board and
Investment Board (application/election-based).
Funding No public budget process; Niche funding sentiment is a low 57% (14
responses). Flagged.
Discovery No named all-School club fair confirmed; the official list and Get Involved page
are the documented entry points.
Why These Three Are Combined
This dossier merges governance/formation, funding, and discovery. The official Upper School list strengthens the
formation picture considerably; funding and a named discovery event remain thin, so they are folded in here with
gaps marked rather than split into near-empty documents.
Governance & Formation
The official Upper School Club List settles the formation question directly: it states that each year, students
initiate the creation of new clubs, pursuing interests beyond the classroom, and that clubs are intended to
develop student leadership, communication, and innovation. Every club pairs faculty advisor(s) with student
leaders — the consistent structural model. The list itself is explicitly described as a living document updated
through a named faculty coordinator as leadership shifts during the year. [Source: Upper School Club List
'25–26]
Formal governance bodies include the elected Student Council and Honor Council, plus the
application/election-based Foundation Board and Investment Board. [Source: Upper School Club List '25–26]
Remaining gap: while the list confirms students start clubs annually and that each needs a faculty advisor, the School does not publish
the step-by-step approval mechanics (sponsoring office, minimum membership, charter timeline). The ethos and advisor requirement are
documented; the procedure is not.
Funding & Budget Process
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
PROVIDENCE DAY SCHOOL CHARGERS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
This remains the thinnest area. Providence Day does not publish a club budget process or per-club allocations.
The only signal is third-party sentiment, and it is comparatively low: on Niche, just 57% of respondents agreed
clubs get the funding they need (only 14 responses). That is too small a sample for a firm conclusion, but low
enough relative to the School's other club sentiment (93% 'plenty of clubs') to note honestly rather than smooth
over. [Source: Niche — Providence Day School]
Honest position: no club funding figures or budget process are asserted; the 57% sentiment is reported only with its small-sample limit.
Discovery & Access
Discovery is partly documented. The official Upper School Club List itself — distributed to students with
advisor and student-leader contacts — is a primary discovery tool, complemented by the School's Get Involved
page and the student portal. A named, all-School club fair or activities showcase is not confirmed in public
sources; it may exist internally but is not claimed here without a source. The student-led formation culture also
aids discovery, since the menu expands to match student interest. [Sources: Upper School Club List '25–26;
providenceday.org — Get Involved]
Gap flagged: a formal club-fair/showcase event is neither confirmed nor denied by public sources; the club list, Get Involved page, and
portal are the documented access points.
Operational Summary
Providence Day's club operations are student-led and advisor-supported, with elected Student and Honor
Councils and an explicit, School-stated culture of students starting new clubs each year. The back-office
specifics — exact approval procedure, club budgets, and a named discovery event — remain unpublished, and
the comparatively low funding-sentiment figure is reported as a flagged signal rather than smoothed over.
Source List
1. Providence Day School — Upper School Club List '25–26 (student-initiated formation; advisor+leader model; governance bodies).
2. Niche — Providence Day School (club funding sentiment 57%; 14 responses; accessed June 2026).
3. Providence Day School — The PD Difference: Get Involved (discovery/entry point).
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 2

sections.text:
PROVIDENCE DAY SCHOOL CHARGERS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Participation & Popularity
Research Area — How many students take part, and which clubs lead
The School itself names affinity groups and service organizations as most popular; a rare School-reported figure puts
nearly half the Upper School in service clubs; and the official list confirms 77 in-scope clubs. Survey sentiment is positive
but small-sample (14 responses).
AT A GLANCE
School's own PDS states its affinity groups and service organizations are among the most
popularity statement popular organizations on campus.
Service participation Nearly half the Upper School takes part in service clubs — voluntary, with no
mandated hours.
Breadth 77 in-scope Upper School clubs confirmed on the official list — a very wide
menu.
Survey sentiment On Niche, 93% agreed there are plenty of clubs and 86% agreed many
participate (only 14 responses).
Most-profile DECA, by its 2026 advance to nationals.
competitive
What the Data Shows
Providence Day publishes more usable signal than most peer schools. With the official Upper School list now in
hand, three things are clear: which categories the School itself calls most popular, a rare hard
service-participation figure, and small-sample survey sentiment.
Most Popular — in the School's Own Words
Unusually, Providence Day states its own popularity read directly on the official club list: its affinity groups and
service organizations are among the most popular organizations on campus. That is a School-stated
qualitative ranking (not a membership count), and it aligns with the service participation figure below and the
nine-group affinity slate documented in the catalog. [Source: Upper School Club List '25–26]
The Strongest Figure: Service Participation
The clearest hard statistic concerns service: Providence Day reports that its Upper School service clubs engage
nearly half of the division's population, on a voluntary basis with no mandated-hours requirement. That
voluntary near-half engagement is a meaningful signal of genuine opt-in club culture. [Source: PDS magazine —
A Culture of Giving]
Breadth as a Participation Signal
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
PROVIDENCE DAY SCHOOL CHARGERS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
The official list confirms 77 in-scope clubs in the Upper School alone. A menu that wide, with clubs meeting as
part of school life and students free to start their own, is itself evidence that participation is broad — the offerings
exist because students populate and lead them. [Source: Upper School Club List '25–26]
Survey Sentiment
On Niche, Providence Day respondents were broadly positive: 93% agreed there are plenty of clubs and 86%
agreed many students participate — but from only 14 self-selected responses, so these indicate sentiment, not a
measured rate. A third item, funding adequacy at 57%, is notably lower and is examined in the Governance
dossier. [Source: Niche — Providence Day School]
Small-sample caveat applied: 14 responses cannot support a precise participation rate; no non-sport club participation percentage is
asserted beyond the School's service figure.
Source List
1. Providence Day School — Upper School Club List '25–26 (most-popular categories; 77 in-scope clubs).
2. PDS magazine — 'A Culture of Giving' (nearly half of Upper School in service clubs; voluntary ethos).
3. Niche — Providence Day School (club sentiment; 14 responses; accessed June 2026).
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 2

PROVIDENCE DAY SCHOOL CHARGERS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Service, Leadership & Civic Engagement
Research Area — Service clubs, student governance, and civic life
Providence Day's defining cluster: the Students of Service network (nearly half the Upper School, voluntary) plus a wide
on-list service slate, Freedom School, Round Square global service, elected Student and Honor Councils, and nine
affinity/alliance groups.
AT A GLANCE
Umbrella Students of Service (SOS) coordinates dozens of student-led service clubs.
Scale Nearly half the Upper School participates; the network has run 20+ years.
Ethos Voluntary — no mandated service hours.
On-list service clubs Charger Guides, Comfort Club, Lower School Buddies, Random Acts of
Kindness, Soccer & Service, Students for Students, Wing Haven,
Microfinance.
Global service Round Square international service (South Africa 2025; Thailand build
project).
Governance bodies Elected Student Council and Honor Council; nine affinity/alliance groups.
A Service-Centered Club Culture
Service is the heart of Providence Day's club life and, the School says, among its most popular. It is delivered
through the Students of Service (SOS) network — dozens of student-led service clubs engaging nearly half the
Upper School, voluntarily and without mandated hours — plus a wide set of service and mentorship clubs on the
official Upper School list. [Sources: PDS magazine — A Culture of Giving; Upper School Club List '25–26]
Service Clubs on the Official List
Beyond the broader SOS network and its named partners (Crisis Assistance Ministry, Bright Blessings, Sparks
Cards, Cards for Kindness, Key Club, Red Cross), the '25–26 Upper School list adds a wide service and
mentorship slate:
Club Focus
Charger Guides Student ambassador/guide group supporting School events.
Comfort Club Comfort, wellbeing, and peer support.
Lower School Buddies Mentoring younger Lower School students.
Random Acts of Kindness Organized small acts of kindness across campus.
Soccer & Service Club (Footy & Facts) Service paired with soccer interest.
Students for Students Peer support and student advocacy.
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
PROVIDENCE DAY SCHOOL CHARGERS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Club Focus
Wing Haven Environmental and garden-stewardship service.
Microfinance Club Small-scale lending and financial-empowerment service.
Source: Upper School Club List '25–26, plus PDS magazine for the SOS network.
Signature Service Initiatives
School-wide efforts include the Freedom School literacy partnership for K–8 students from underserved
Charlotte communities (over a dozen students earned national recognition in 2024), the Gil Murdock Turkey
Trot food-and-supplies drive (9,757 items in 2021), an annual toy drive, and issue-based responses such as
Hurricane Helene relief drives. [Sources: providenceday.org — news; PDS magazine; alumni news]
Global Service — Round Square
As a Round Square member school, Providence Day links service to its global identity through international
service and exchange — a 2025 community-service trip to South Africa and an earlier Thailand project that
helped build a research center, park ranger huts, and lookout towers. [Source: providenceday.org — Global
Education]
Leadership, Governance & Identity
Formal governance runs through the elected Student Council and the Honor Council, with the Foundation
Board and Investment Board as additional application/election-based leadership bodies. Identity and belonging
are served by nine affinity/alliance groups — AMEMSA, AAPI, Black Student Union, Diabuddies, Fellowship of
Christian Athletes, Gender & Sexuality Alliance, Hispanic/Latinx, Jewish Culture Club, and SAGE — supported
by a full-time Chief Diversity Officer. [Sources: Upper School Club List '25–26; providenceday.org — Equity,
Inclusion, and Belonging]
Civic-Engagement Read
Providence Day's civic identity is service-forward: a large, voluntary, student-led service apparatus and a broad
affinity slate, complemented by elected Student and Honor Councils and the global-citizenship framing of the
Global Studies Diploma. The competitive civic clubs (Speech & Debate, Mock Trial, Model U.N.) add a
public-voice dimension covered in the Academic & Competitive dossier.

2. Providence Day School — Upper School Club List '25–26 (service, leadership, affinity rosters).
3. Providence Day School — news & alumni news (Freedom School 2024; Gil Murdock Turkey Trot).
4. Providence Day School — Global Education (Round Square; South Africa 2025; Thailand project).
5. Providence Day School — Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (affinity groups; Chief Diversity Officer).
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 2

Thematic Pathways
Research Area — What clusters of clubs expose students to, and how
Six pathways: signature global & cultural, a large service slate, a standout business/finance pipeline (DECA, FBLA,
investing, economics), a serious civic/pre-law cluster (debate, mock trial, Model U.N.), STEM & innovation, and
identity/wellbeing. Exposure, not outcome promises.
AT A GLANCE
Global & Cultural Model U.N., World Quest, five+ language/culture clubs, the Global Studies
Diploma, PD Passport, and Round Square.
Service & Civic A broad service slate plus the elected Honor Council and Student Council —
the School's largest cluster.
Business & Finance DECA, FBLA, Investment Management Society, Microfinance, Investment
Board, Euro Challenge, PD Economics Challenge.
Civic Voice / Law Speech & Debate, Mock Trial, Model U.N., World Quest, Quiz Bowl, Criminal
Justice Club.
STEM & Innovation Science Olympiad, Robotics, TSA, Drone, Build Your Own Boat, AI/ML,
Coding, Women in STEM, the IDEAS makerspaces.
Identity & Wellbeing Nine affinity/alliance groups plus wellness clubs (Meditation, Comfort).
How Clubs Cluster Into Pathways
With the full Upper School roster confirmed, Providence Day's non-sport, non-arts activities resolve into six clear
pathways. Each is framed as exposure and demonstrated interest, not a promise of any outcome. The global
and service pathways remain the School's signature, but the official list reveals an unusually strong
business/finance pathway and a deep civic-competition pathway as well.
Pathway 1 — Global & Cultural Exposure (the Signature)
Global education remains Providence Day's defining identity. PDS built the nation's first Global Studies
Diploma, runs the TK–12 PD Passport, and is a Round Square member school with international service
(South Africa 2025; an earlier Thailand build project). The club roster feeds this directly: Model U.N. and World
Quest on the competitive side, and a deep set of language and culture clubs — Chinese, French, German,
Spanish, Italian, plus Latin Club and the Greek Society, and the International Food Club. [Sources:
providenceday.org — Global Education; Upper School Club List '25–26]
Pathway 2 — Service & Civic Engagement
Service remains the largest cluster, anchored by the Students of Service network and reinforced on the official
list by clubs such as Charger Guides, Comfort Club, Lower School Buddies, Random Acts of Kindness, Soccer &
Service, Students for Students, Wing Haven, and Microfinance. It is treated in full in the Service, Leadership &
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
PROVIDENCE DAY SCHOOL CHARGERS — STUDENT CLUBS & ACTIVITIES RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Civic Engagement dossier. [Source: Upper School Club List '25–26]
Pathway 3 — Business & Finance (a Standout)
The official list reveals a business and finance pathway unusually deep for an independent school: DECA
(competition), Future Business Leaders of America, the Investment Management Society, the Microfinance
Club, the Investment Board, and two economics competitions (Euro Challenge and the PD Economics
Challenge). For a student oriented toward business, finance, or entrepreneurship, this is a genuine multi-club
pipeline with a competitive outlet. [Source: Upper School Club List '25–26]
Pathway 4 — Civic Voice, Law & Policy
A serious civic and pre-law pathway runs through Speech & Debate, Mock Trial, Model U.N., World Quest,
and Quiz Bowl, with the Criminal Justice Club and the elected Honor Council adding law-and-governance
exposure. This cluster builds argument, evidence, public speaking, and deliberation — the skills associated with
law, government, and policy. [Source: Upper School Club List '25–26]
Pathway 5 — STEM & Innovation
The STEM pathway pairs competition with making: Science Olympiad, the Robotics Team, TSA, Drone Club,
and Build Your Own Boat on the competitive/engineering side, and AI / Machine Learning, Coding (Swift), the
Computer Science Honors Society, Science Club, and Women in STEM on the exploratory side — reinforced
by the Middle School IDEAS makerspaces. [Source: Upper School Club List '25–26]
Pathway 6 — Identity & Wellbeing
Nine affinity and alliance groups (AMEMSA, AAPI, BSU, Diabuddies, FCA, GSA, Hispanic/Latinx, JCC, SAGE)
build community and belonging — which the School identifies among its most popular organizations —
complemented by wellness clubs such as Meditation and Comfort. [Source: Upper School Club List '25–26]
Reading the Pathways Honestly
These clusters describe exposure, not outcomes. The best-validated pathways remain global and service
(dedicated programs, a first-in-nation diploma, a School-reported participation figure), but the official roster
shows the business/finance and civic-competition pathways are genuine, multi-club strengths rather than token
offerings.
Source List
1. Providence Day School — Upper School Club List '25–26 (full roster underpinning every pathway).
2. Providence Day School — Global Education (Global Studies Diploma, PD Passport, Round Square).
3. Providence Day School — IDEAS@PD (Middle School STEM makerspaces).
Compiled June 24, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 2

# Providence Day School — Student Clubs Redesign Deep Research

redesign (cards 1a Affinity & Identity Groups, 1b Service & Civic Engagement,
1c Honor Societies). Method: live fetches of providenceday.org plus Wayback Machine
captures for pages lost in the site's `/about/…` → `/the-pd-difference/…` migration.

**Confidence key.** VERIFIED = read from a live page. ARCHIVED = read from a dated Wayback
capture because the live page 404s. NOT FOUND = explicitly searched and absent.

**Site-migration caveat (load-bearing).** Providence Day restructured its site, and the
pages that *enumerate* affinity groups now return 404. Re-checked live on 2026-07-26: the
EIB landing page returns **HTTP 200 but names no affinity groups** (they appear only as four
unlabeled image tiles), while the roster page returns **HTTP 404**. The enumerated roster
below therefore comes from dated Wayback captures, and the live page's silence is itself the
gap flag on card 1a.

---

sections.text:
**Structural finding:** Providence Day's identity groups sit under a **DEI umbrella (the
Office of Equity, Inclusion & Belonging)**, *not* under global engagement. Global Education
is a separate department with its own leadership. This settles the question the research
brief raised.

### The umbrella — VERIFIED

**Office of Equity, Inclusion & Belonging (EIB)**, led by **Tyrone Jean**, Assistant Head of
School for EIB and Chief Diversity Officer. Staffing: 1 Assistant Head + 2 Associate
Directors + 6 faculty coordinators. The office's founding year is **not published**.
→ https://www.providenceday.org/the-pd-difference/equity-inclusion-and-belonging

### The enumerated roster with founding years — ARCHIVED

From the "Connectivity" page, captured **2025-03-13**:
https://web.archive.org/web/20250313123919/https://www.providenceday.org/about/equity-inclusion/office-of-equity-inclusion-summary-report/connectivity

**Upper School (9)**
- Fellowship of Christian Athletes (1995)
- Gender and Sexuality Alliance (2015, formerly HRA)
- Black Student Union (2016)
- Asian Affinity Group (2017)
- Jewish Culture Club (2017)
- SAGE — Students Advocating for Gender Equality (2017)
- Multiracial Affinity Group (2017)
- Hispanic/Latinx Affinity Group (2018)
- AMEMSA — Arab, Middle Eastern, Muslim, and South Asian Affinity Group (2020)

**Middle School (2)**
- Diversity Club (2018)
- CEED — Council for Education on Equity and Diversity (2020)

**Lower School (2)**
- Kaleidoscope, 5th grade (2019) — an equity and social-justice learning space
- African-American and Asian Affinity Group, grades 4–5 (2020)

**Faculty (2)** — Faculty of Color Group (2018); AWARE — Alliance of White Anti-Racist
Educators (2019). **Alumni (1)** — AFIRM (2020).

**Newer groups** added per the 2022 annual report, captured **2023-12-13**: Jewish Student
Association, **Rainbow Alliance** (Middle School), and a Jewish Affinity Group (Lower
School). →
https://web.archive.org/web/20231213140845/https://www.providenceday.org/about/equity-inclusion/2022-annual-report-on-equity-inclusion-and-belonging/inclusion

### Parent groups — ARCHIVED

- **Anti-Racist Task Force** (2020) — parent-led, evolved from the Multicultural Advisory
 Board
- **Black Families Network** and **Hispanic Families Network** (both 2021)
- The Parents' Association **Cultural Connections committee** — hosts Diwali, Hanukkah,
 Lunar New Year, and Eid al-Fitr

### The leadership arm — ARCHIVED

**Student Diversity Council (2017)** — the liaison between students and Upper School
administrators.

### GSA detail — VERIFIED

"Over 40 active members"; partners with Time Out Youth; runs a campus-wide Rainbow Day each
April. →
https://www.providenceday.org/about/pd-communications/news-media/post/~board/news-media/post/upper-school-gsa-supports-time-out-youth

### Flags — 1a

**GAP (not a count discrepancy).** There is **no advertised "N affinity groups" figure** to
conflict with the roster. The live EIB page, the "Why Providence Day" admissions page, Get
Involved, and the archived reports were all checked: the live EIB page presents affinity
groups as **four image tiles** (Lower School / Middle School / Upper School / Families,
Faculty, and Staff) with no names and no count in the HTML. So the honest flag here is that
the school's own live site no longer enumerates the groups it runs — the roster survives only
in archive.

**One genuine internal inconsistency worth flagging:** the archived Upper School list
contains a **duplicate Black Student Union entry with two different years — "Black Student
Union, 2017" and "Black Student Union (2016)"** — on PD's own page (same URL as the roster
above).

**NOT FOUND:** no published PD source confirms SDLC / NAIS Student Diversity Leadership
Conference attendance. (A search hit for SDLC was **Providence High School**, a different
school — excluded.) The coordinators post references faculty attending the People of Color
Conference for professional development, with no numbers.

sections.text:
### Program 1 — Providence Day Freedom School — scale: 55 scholars; founded 2012; a national first

**"The first independent school in the country to host a CDF Freedom School"** and "the only
independent school in the nation to host a Freedom School program each summer." A summer
literacy program for K–8 Charlotte scholars, run in partnership with Freedom School
Partners. The community collects supplies for all **18 Charlotte Freedom School sites**.

- Sources: https://www.providenceday.org/about/freedom-school ·
 https://web.archive.org/web/20250407090326/https://www.providenceday.org/about/social-responsibility

### Program 2 — Community Engagement / President's Volunteer Service Award — scale: 5,247 hours in one year

**5,247 service hours in a single school year; 20,642 hours since 2017; 48 students earned
the award in 2024** (24 Gold, 5 Silver, 9 Bronze). Led by Jennifer Bratyanski, Upper School
Community Engagement Coordinator. Named partners: Wayfinders, RecycleBalls, Charlotte
Mecklenburg Library, Mecklenburg County Teen Court, Augustine Literacy Project, and National
Charity League.

- Source: https://www.providenceday.org/about/pd-communications/news-media/post/~board/news-media/post/students-earn-national-honor-while-serving-their-community

### Program 3 — Round Square — scale: joined 2016; the only member school in North Carolina

A network of **250+ schools in 50 countries** built on the IDEALS framework (International
understanding, Democracy, Environmental stewardship, Adventure, Leadership, **Service**),
including international service projects ("Big Builds") and exchanges.

- Source: https://www.providenceday.org/the-pd-difference/global-education

### Additional scale figure — VERIFIED

"Over **30 student-run service clubs**." →
https://www.providenceday.org/admissions/why-providence-day

### "Individual activity, not a club" — ARCHIVED

Curricular or divisional initiatives and individual recognition, **not** standalone clubs
(all from the archived Community Engagement page above):

- 9th-grade **Charger Impact Challenge** — a grade-level initiative
- Grade-level partnerships: 6th → Movement School; 7th → Winterfield Elementary;
 8th → Wilson STEM Academy
- Lower School service exposure: Levine Children's Hospital, The Lunch Project, Fifth Grade
 Safety Patrol, Collateral Repair Project, The Relatives, Ronald McDonald House, Crisis
 Assistance Ministries
- **US Community Engagement Portal** — an opportunity-listing tool
- **Student-led Foundation Board** — described as a student-led body, not explicitly a club
- The **President's Volunteer Service Award** itself — an *individual* recognition of hours

**UNCONFIRMED, excluded:** voter-education internships appeared in a search snippet but could
not be verified on any live PD page.

sections.text:
### The roster — VERIFIED (five, all Upper School)

| Society | Division | What it recognizes | Feeds from |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cum Laude Society** | Upper School | "Superior scholastic achievement in secondary schools"; motto excellence, justice, honor | The classroom |
| **National Honor Society** | Upper School | Scholarship, leadership, service, character | Classroom + service |
| **National Art Honor Society** | Upper School | Visual-arts achievement and service | The Arts — visual |
| **Tri-M Music Honor Society** | Upper School | Music achievement and leadership; a NAfME program | The Arts — music |
| **Société Honoraire de Français** | Upper School | French achievement; "the high school equivalent of Pi Delta Phi" | World languages |

Sources (each society is evidenced by its own news post):
- Cum Laude: https://www.providenceday.org/about/pd-communications/news-media/post/~board/news-media/post/pd-celebrates-34-new-members-of-the-cum-laude-society
- NHS: https://www.providenceday.org/cf_news/view.cfm?newsid=2101
- Tri-M: https://www.providenceday.org/about/pd-communications/news-media/post/~board/news-media/post/eleven-upper-school-students-inducted-into-tri-m-music-honor-society

### Induction criteria — only NHS publishes them

**National Honor Society:** "Selection is based on four criteria: scholarship, leadership,
service and character," plus attendance at PDS for a minimum of one year and a **cumulative
GPA of 3.6 or higher**; selection by a faculty committee.

### Published induction counts — news posts only, not a standing page

- **NHS: 89 inducted** (8 seniors, 81 juniors), Nov 8 2017, joining 81 existing members
- **Cum Laude: 34** (2022), **31**, and **29** (2018) in separate years
- **National Art Honor Society: nearly 50** in May; the chapter was added "in the last five
 years" per the admissions page; service projects at Wing Haven and Daniel Stowe Botanical
 Garden
- **Tri-M: 11 inducted**, Nov 2019; chapter established **2016**; advisor Sarah Russell

### GAP FLAG — 1c

- **No standing honor-societies page exists** on providenceday.org. Every fact above comes
 from one-off news posts, so the counts are historical rather than current.
- **Induction criteria are not published for Cum Laude, NAHS, Tri-M, or Société Honoraire de
 Français** — only for NHS.
- **Annual induction counts are not published systematically.**

### NOT FOUND — explicitly searched

**National Junior Honor Society, Quill & Scroll, Rho Kappa, Mu Alpha Theta, Science NHS**,
and any **Spanish / Latin / Chinese** honor society. Targeted CDX archive searches for
`rho-kappa`, `mu-alpha`, `quill`, `junior-honor`, and `spanish-honor` across the full
providenceday.org URL history returned **zero hits**. Notably **no Middle School honor
society** could be confirmed at all — and despite PD offering five world languages, only the
French society is evidenced.

### Method note for future ingests

The 2025-26 Upper School Course of Study PDF
(https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1759758182/provday/wekh9bxtsqah5givkjk2/2025-2026UpperSchoolCourseofStudy.pdf)
is a **scanned, image-based PDF with no text layer**, so it could not be searched for honor
societies. Reading it via OCR is the highest-value next step for certainty on the missing
societies (especially Spanish/Latin/Chinese and any Middle School society).
